gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S, sold as a '55 pints/day (AHAM)' unit, is federally rated at 36.33 pints/day and 2.08 L/kWh under the DOE Appendix X1 portable test at 65°F / 60% RH, which is about two-thirds of the AHAM 80°F figure every rival page sizes on.
standout_why: dehumidifierverdict.com (cited in both chats) gives the HDi65/HDi65S only as 120 PPD saturation and 55 AHAM. It never mentions a DOE or 65°F rating and gives no efficiency figure. crawlspacedehumidifiers.org/with-pump (cited) says 'none of these manufacturers publish a DOE 65°F figure'. It marks the HDi65S as ENERGY STAR but gives no DOE pints or IEF for it, and it has 65°F/73°F figures only for other models (NXT85C 49 pints at 65°F, HDi100 78 and HDi120 93 at 73°F). crawlclimate.com/best/built-in-pump (cited) would not load (TLS certificate error), so I could not check it. Our own page lists AHAM only. Rivals cover part of the AHAM-versus-DOE idea, but not for the unit ChatGPT recommended.
decides: This confirms the picks but changes the sizing advice. A crawl space at about 65°F is close to the DOE test room, and there the '55-pint' HDi65S removes about 36 pints/day (66% of its AHAM figure). A buyer with a cool or wet crawl near the 1,300 sq ft coverage claim should move up a size (Galaxy 85P or HDi90) rather than trust the AHAM number. It also corrects the pump column. On AlorAir's own spec tables, the 19.6 ft figure on the HD55P and Galaxy 85P is labelled 'Drain Hose Length'. It is not a stated lift, so our 'drain height' cell and rivals' '19.6 ft lift' need a footnote.

findings.note: Same record as above. AlorAir's HDi90 'COP 2.69 L/kWh' has no stated test conditions, so the two numbers can't be compared directly.

findings.label: DOE test conditions behind ENERGY STAR / federal dehumidifier ratings
findings.value: Portable: 65°F dry bulb, 60% RH; whole-home: 73°F dry bulb, 60% RH
findings.source_title: 10 CFR Appendix X1 to Subpart B of Part 430, Table 1 (Cornell LII)
findings.note: Section 4.1.1, Table 1: portable 65 ± 2.0°F, 60 ± 2% RH; whole-home 73 ± 2.0°F, 60 ± 2% RH. The AHAM figure all rival pages use is taken at 80°F / 60% RH, per dehumidifierverdict.com and crawlspacedehumidifiers.org.
